title: Zero-dep SDK Minilab and Instrumentation Journal
content:
Purpose
This is a intentionally lightweight lab and working journal for a zero-dependency (zero-dep) SDK quickstart: the goal is to get an engineer from 0 -> observable demo in ~30 minutes, and a reproducible 1-hour minilab with instrumentation and failure-mode checks. This doc captures the fast path, instrumentation checklist, demo script, and open questions that came up during an experiment session.

Intended audience
- Developer advocates running workshops
- SDK engineers building starter kits and sample apps
- Solutions engineers preparing a short demo for evaluation calls

Non-goals
- Not a full API reference or security hardening checklist.
- Not intended to replace the canonical SDK README or the API docs.

High-level constraints and assumptions
- Zero-dep means: no preinstalled packages beyond the language runtime. The sample uses raw HTTP calls (curl/node fetch) and a single-file helper if needed.
- Polyglot coverage: show JS (node), Python, and a tiny cURL flow.
- No auth complexity: use an ephemeral API key injected at runtime (WORKSHOP_KEY env var).
- Telemetry must be visible in 30 minutes: we push minimal metrics to a staging metrics endpoint (mock Prometheus pushgateway or a simple webhook that writes to a shared log).

Quick checklist (30-min demo)
1) Environment prep (5 min)
   - Open terminal, set WORKSHOP_KEY=<key from console>
   - Ensure node or python is installed (versions called out in preamble)
2) cURL smoke test (2 min)
   - curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-internal.test/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $WORKSHOP_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rlm-mini-1","input":"Hello world"}'
3) Python minimal (8 min)
   - one-file: tiny_client.py (no pip). Uses urllib.request to POST JSON. Print response and timing.
4) JS minimal (8 min)
   - node 18+ built-in fetch example in one file sample.js. Measures latency, prints tokens (if returned).
5) Telemetry on-view (5 min)
   - run the sample with METRICS_STAGING=https://push-test.internal.local and watch the staging console (shared tab).
6) Demo wrap-up and show logs/trace (2 min)
   - point to Console -> per-route traces, show request counts and a single failed request example.

Detailed 1-hour minilab flow (expand the quick checklist)
- Phase A: Local smoke + negative tests (20 min)\  - Successful 5 requests: baseline times, token outputs, small prompt variations\  - One deliberate bad payload to surface 400/422 errors\  - One auth failure (empty key) to show clear error messaging and guidance
- Phase B: Add minimal retry and fallback (15 min)\  - Show a 3-call fallback to a smaller cheaper model if latency > target\  - Instrument retry counts to telemetry and verify they show up in staging metrics
- Phase C: Prefix caching demo (10 min)\  - Use a local in-memory map to cache a warm prefix. Run 10 requests with repeated prefix, show reduced latency and lower token usage in logs\- Phase D: Rollout & feature flag demo (10 min)\  - Show how to swap from the default model to a canary via a single header X-Model-ID and how Console rollout widgets reflect traffic split\- Phase E: Postmortem quick notes (5 min)\  - Capture one-sentence learnings and next steps

Code snippets (one-file minimal)
- Python (tiny_client.py)
  import os, time, json, urllib.request
  KEY = os.getenv('WORKSHOP_KEY')
  body = json.dumps({"model":"rlm-mini-1","input":"Summarize: quickstart"}).encode('utf-8')
  req = urllib.request.Request('https://api.redwood-internal.test/v1/generate', data=body, headers={ 'Authorization': f'Bearer {KEY}', 'Content-Type':'application/json'})
  t0 = time.time(); r = urllib.request.urlopen(req); print('status', r.getcode()); print('elapsed', time.time()-t0); print(r.read().decode())

- Node (sample.js)
  const key = process.env.WORKSHOP_KEY
  const body = JSON.stringify({model: 'rlm-mini-1', input: 'Explain the principle of least astonishment'})
  (async ()=>{ const t0 = Date.now(); const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood-internal.test/v1/generate', {method: 'POST', headers: {'Authorization': `Bearer ${key}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}, body}); const latency = Date.now()-t0; console.log('latency_ms', latency); console.log(await res.text());})()

Instrumentation and observable signals (must be visible during the lab)
- Metrics to push (minimum): request_count, request_latency_ms_bucket, error_count, model_id, retry_count\- Telemetry sink options for the workshop:\  - pushgateway mock (local docker) -> show Prometheus graph (recommended)\  - webhook to simple staging logger -> prints in Console shared page\  - use Console's ingestion demo token (if available)
- Traces: add a trace-id header X-Trace-Id and echo it in server responses so demo participants can grep logs
- Logs: request id, model, input hash (not raw prompt for privacy), latency, status_code

Sample telemetry payload (HTTP POST)
{
  "metric":"request_latency",
  "value_ms":128,
  "labels":{ "model":"rlm-mini-1","team":"workshop" },
  "ts":"2025-01-20T15:12:00Z"
}
(When implementing, we serialize as a one-line JSON to the staging webhook.)

Failure modes to highlight and how to teach them
- Cold KV cache -> higher latency on first sample: show dramatic difference and explain KV caching behavior
- Rate limited -> 429, show how SDK should surface this, backoff example (expo capped)
- Model quality regression -> show a bad prompt dataset and tie to Optimize's evals workflow

Runbook snippets for SEs running the lab
- If staging metrics disappear: check pushgateway container -> docker logs; fallback to webhook
- If API key rejected: ensure WORKSHOP_KEY is set, paste a fresh key from the console test tokens page
- If demo returns long latency: check selected model in header, if canary model is heavy switch to low-cost model with X-Model-ID

Open questions / follow-ups (to turn into tidy tasks)
- Should the zero-dep samples include a prewired tiny wasm binary for fast hashing rather than input hashing in Python? (Pro: consistent speed; Con: increases artifact count)
- Do we allow workshop participants to push telemetry to a shared staging sink (privacy)? Or should we provide an isolated per-team sink?
- How to best show token accounting without exposing raw prompt contents (masking strategy)?

Session notes (raw, informal)
- 2025-01-20 14:00 — ran through the flow with Jonah and Priya. The node flow is the fastest to demo because fetch is builtin and async logs look nice.
- 2025-01-20 14:30 — encountered CORS issue when trying to demo from browser snippet; choose node instead for the live session and keep browser snippet for follow-up lab doc.
- 2025-01-20 15:00 — telemetry webhook needed small schema tweak (labels flattened). Will update sample scripts.

Suggested artifacts to land from this doc (next actions)
- [ ] one-file samples bundle (python/node/curl) in repo: sdk-examples/zero-dep-minilab
- [ ] small docker-compose for pushgateway mock + tiny web UI
- [ ] workshop slide 1-pager listing commands and run checklist (handout)

Links & references (internal)
- GH PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-prototypes/pull/182
- Jira: RED-2314 (minilab and telemetry sprint)
- Slack: #devexp-workshops thread id: C12345WSP

Appendix: teaching script (30-min variant)
- 0:00 — 0:05 intro to goal and what zero-dep means
- 0:05 — 0:10 run cURL and show a successful response
- 0:10 — 0:18 run Python then Node samples (explain timing differences)
- 0:18 — 0:22 show telemetry sink receiving metrics
- 0:22 — 0:27 run one fallback scenario and show Console rollout switch
- 0:27 — 0:30 quick Q&A and next steps (link to repo and follow-up lab)

End of journal entry.

(Notes to self: convert this into a tidy README and a slide handout; remove sensitive staging URLs before publishing.)
